input.strategy_title: Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview and adoption is strong, but enterprise
customers will not build production GenAI applications on a TP component.
Graduating to GA requires API stability commitments, a production support
posture, and closing the quality gaps that TP status currently excuses. The
full inventory of those gaps is not yet known — TP feedback is scattered across
support tickets, and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. |
| HLR-3 | P0 | Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. |
| HLR-5 | P1 | The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). |
| HLR-6 | P2 | Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including migration notes from TP. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- TrustyAI
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- New Llama Stack feature development beyond GA-bar quality work
- Deprecating alternative GenAI serving paths

## Open Questions

1. The GA scope itself depends on HLR-1's assessment — until it lands, the
   size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate.

# Llama Stack GA-readiness assessment

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's central unknown: no systematic GA-readiness
assessment of Llama Stack has been done, and the full inventory of gaps
between current Tech Preview quality and the GA bar is not known. This
investigation produces the definitive GA scope — a prioritized, sized
inventory of quality gaps across API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits,
and error handling — that determines the scope of the downstream stability,
hardening, and support-posture work.

## Scope

- Audit the published Llama Stack API surface (LlamaStackDistribution CRD and
  the OpenAI-compatible REST APIs) against GA stability requirements,
  identifying unstable or undocumented surface area.
- Evaluate the upgrade path from the last two Tech Preview releases,
  identifying breakage and missing migration coverage.
- Assess scale limits (concurrent distributions, request throughput, provider
  saturation) against enterprise production expectations, using TP feedback
  scattered across support tickets as an input.
- Review error handling and failure modes across the distribution's
  components (inference provider, storage, operator reconciliation).
- Consolidate TP feedback from support tickets into structured findings.
- Produce the GA scope document: a prioritized gap inventory with severity,
  remediation recommendation, and rough sizing per gap, ratifying what is in
  and out of the GA bar.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An assessment report exists covering all four gap areas (API stability,
  upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), with each finding classified
  by severity and including a remediation recommendation and rough sizing.
- TP feedback from support tickets has been consolidated into the report's
  findings, with no known TP feedback source left unreviewed.
- A GA scope document is produced that enumerates the gaps that must close
  for GA and explicitly defers gaps that fall outside the GA bar, and it has
  been reviewed with product and engineering stakeholders.
- The gap inventory is sufficient for the downstream stability and hardening
  work, and for the support-posture work, to be scoped without re-deriving
  the analysis.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between
  current TP quality and the GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale
  limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. This epic is
  the direct deliverer of HLR-1.

# Llama Stack API stability guarantees and GA hardening

## Description

This epic delivers the API stability guarantee that GA requires for Llama
Stack: versioned APIs, an enforced deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade
path from the last two Tech Preview releases. It also remediates the quality
gaps (scale limits, error handling, and other GA-bar gaps) identified by the
GA-readiness assessment, closing the quality deficit that Tech Preview
status currently excuses.

## Scope

- Introduce API versioning across the published Llama Stack surface
  (LlamaStackDistribution CRD and the OpenAI-compatible REST APIs).
- Implement the deprecation policy mechanism: deprecated surface is
  identified, communicated, and retained for the documented grace period.
- Build and automate upgrade-path testing covering migration from the last
  two Tech Preview releases to the GA release.
- Remediate the GA-bar quality gaps recorded in the GA-readiness assessment
  (expected to include scale limits and error handling/failure-mode
  coverage); each remediation follows the assessment's recommendation unless
  a documented decision defers it with rationale.
- Update in-repo references (examples, captions, doc pointers) that fall out
  of these changes — incidental touch-ups only; the GA documentation uplift
  is handled separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The published API surface carries explicit version identifiers, and the
  versioning scheme is documented.
- The deprecation policy is documented and mechanically enforced: use of
  deprecated surface produces the documented warning/behavior during the
  grace period.
- An automated upgrade-path test migrates a distribution from each of the
  last two Tech Preview releases to the GA release and passes.
- Every gap item in the ratified GA scope that falls in this epic's areas
  (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling) is either
  remediated or explicitly deferred with a recorded rationale accepted by
  stakeholders.
- All changes merge through a green Konflux build pipeline for the
  llama-stack midstream repo.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: Published API surface carries a stability guarantee —
  versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the
  last two TP releases. This epic is the direct deliverer of HLR-2.
- Assessment-driven gap remediation (the actionable output of HLR-1) is
  bundled here: it edits the same API/quality surface of the same component
  and team as the stability work, so it is not a separately schedulable
  deliverable.

# Llama Stack production support posture

## Description

This epic puts the production support posture in place that GA requires:
documented SLO targets, a backport policy, and a supported configuration
matrix for Llama Stack. These are the support-engineering deliverables that
let enterprise customers run Llama Stack in production with defined
expectations.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the GA Llama Stack distribution
  (availability and operational service levels), aligned to the ratified GA
  scope.
- Define and document the backport policy: which releases receive fixes, for
  how long, and how backports are requested and delivered.
- Define and publish the supported configuration matrix: the provider,
  dependency, and deployment combinations that are supported at GA (e.g.
  inference and vector/storage provider combinations the distribution is
  validated against), reflecting the GA scope and the platform architecture
  context.
- Review the posture documents with support and product stakeholders and
  publish them through the product's support-documentation channels.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets are documented and published for the GA distribution.
- The backport policy is documented and published, covering supported
  release lines and backport request handling.
- The supported configuration matrix is published and covers every
  configuration the ratified GA scope declares supported; configurations
  outside the matrix are explicitly marked unsupported.
- The posture documents have been reviewed and accepted by support and
  product stakeholders.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P0)**: Production support posture is in place — documented SLO
  targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. This epic is
  the direct deliverer of HLR-3.

# TrustyAI guardrails as a supported Llama Stack integration

## Description

This epic promotes safety guardrails via TrustyAI from an experimental flag
to a supported, documented integration for GA Llama Stack distributions.
Enterprise customers building production GenAI applications on the GA
distribution need guardrails as a first-class supported capability, validated
against the versioned GA API surface.

## Scope

- Remove the experimental/opt-in flag gating the TrustyAI guardrails
  integration so it ships as a standard supported capability of GA
  distributions.
- Harden and validate the integration against the versioned GA API surface
  and deprecation policy delivered by the Llama Stack stability work,
  including its behavior across the supported configuration matrix.
- Author the integration documentation (configuration, supported deployment
  topologies, operational guidance) marking it as supported — this is
  integration-specific documentation that belongs to this epic's deliverable,
  distinct from the platform-wide GA documentation uplift.
- Add/extend validation coverage for the integration in the TrustyAI
  operator and integration test suites.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The TrustyAI guardrails integration is available in GA Llama Stack
  distributions without any experimental opt-in flag.
- The integration is validated against the versioned GA API surface and
  across the published supported configuration matrix, and the validation
  passes as part of the integration test suite.
- Integration documentation is published describing configuration and
  supported topologies, marked as a supported (not experimental) capability.
- All changes merge through a green Konflux build pipeline for the TrustyAI
  midstream repo.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P1)**: Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. This epic is
  the direct deliverer of HLR-4.

# Dashboard Llama Stack management enabled by default

## Description

This epic enables Llama Stack management in the Dashboard by default for
entitled clusters, removing the Tech Preview opt-in gate. Entitled users see
Llama Stack management surfaces without configuration, while the change stays
contained to the Dashboard's existing feature-flag and entitlement
mechanisms.

## Scope

- Change the Dashboard feature default so Llama Stack management is enabled
  by default, driven by cluster entitlement (via the Dashboard's existing
  OdhDashboardConfig feature-flag mechanism).
- Remove the Tech Preview opt-in gate for Llama Stack management.
- Preserve an administrator path to disable Llama Stack management via the
  existing configuration mechanism (rollback/disable safety for the default
  flip).
- Update Dashboard tests covering default-on behavior for entitled clusters,
  unaffected behavior for non-entitled clusters, and the disable path.
- Incidental UI text/caption updates that fall out of the default flip are
  included here; no new doc topics are authored in this epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On an entitled cluster with default configuration, Llama Stack management
  surfaces are visible and usable in the Dashboard with no opt-in step.
- On a non-entitled cluster, Llama Stack management remains hidden and no
  errors or degraded behavior result.
- An administrator can disable Llama Stack management through the existing
  configuration mechanism, and the disable is effective after reload.
- Regression tests cover the entitled default-on, non-entitled hidden, and
  administrator-disable paths, and pass.
- All changes merge through a green Konflux build pipeline for the Dashboard
  midstream repo.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-5 (P1)**: The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default
  for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). This epic is the direct
  deliverer of HLR-5.

# Llama Stack GA documentation uplift

## Description

This epic uplifts Llama Stack documentation to GA standards, including
migration notes from Tech Preview. The documentation describes the GA
distribution as built: the versioned API surface, the production support
posture, the supported TrustyAI guardrails integration, and the default-on
Dashboard experience.

## Scope

Content outline (authored within this epic):

- **GA-standard review and rewrite** of the Llama Stack documentation set —
  installation, configuration, and operational topics aligned to the
  published supported configuration matrix and SLO/backport policy.
- **Migration notes from Tech Preview** — a migration guide covering the
  move from the last two TP releases to the GA release, aligned with the
  tested upgrade path.
- **GA positioning updates** — remove Tech Preview caveats and experimental
  labeling from Llama Stack doc topics, including the guardrails integration
  and Dashboard management topics where they reference Llama Stack.
- **Accuracy validation** — every documented procedure, configuration
  reference, and API example validated against the implemented GA behavior
  and the platform architecture context before publication.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Llama Stack documentation set meets GA documentation standards as
  defined by the Red Hat docs content process.
- A migration guide exists covering upgrade from the last two Tech Preview
  releases, consistent with the tested upgrade path delivered by the
  stability work.
- No Llama Stack doc topic describes the component or its guardrails
  integration as Tech Preview or experimental where GA behavior has shipped.
- All documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented GA
  behavior (APIs, support posture, guardrails integration, Dashboard
  defaults) by engineering owners before publication.
- Documentation is published through the Red Hat docs content process.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-6 (P2)**: Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including
  migration notes from TP. This epic is the direct deliverer of HLR-6.
